builder_purity.no_floating_point_arithmetic_on_weights: weights only pass through concatenate (bit-copy) and fancy-index gather; no add/mul/cast (diff inspection)
builder_purity.no_dtype_changes_on_outputs: fast path emits pointer int64 (np.cumsum dtype=int64), neighbors int64, weights float64, is_network bool_ - identical to baseline np.zeros(...,int64)/np.array(...,int64)/np.array(...,float64)/np.array(...,bool_)

order_rule_equivalent.structural_argument: baseline visits nodes 0..V-1 and per node appends forward incidences (start==node) in edge order then reverse incidences (end==node) in edge order; candidate stable-sorts the concatenation [all forward in edge order; all reverse in edge order] by source node - a stable sort preserves input order among equal keys, and every forward incidence lies before every reverse incidence in the concatenated array, so each row is exactly forward-in-edge-order then reverse-in-edge-order
order_rule_equivalent.empirical: 400 randomized adversarial graphs (V in 0..8, E to 25, dense self-loops/parallel edges/isolated nodes/empty graphs, int64 and int32 endpoints, aliased ab/ba weights, weights including -0.0, NaN, +Inf, -Inf, 5e-324, DBL_MAX) compared bit-for-bit (float64 via uint64 views, dtype+shape asserted) against a verbatim transcription of the baseline loops: 0 mismatches; hand-checked 3-node/6-edge case row for node 1 = [0,2,1,0,0,2,1] (self-loop appears in both forward and reverse position)
order_rule_equivalent.parallel_edges_and_self_loops: retained; no dedup anywhere in the builder (measured)

builder_purity.int32_admission_exactness: int32->int64 astype is value-exact and commutes with the stable gather; baseline output is already int64 (list-to-array widening), so observable arrays are identical; measured on 200 int32 randomized graphs (subset of the 400 above)

all four inputs exactly np.ndarray, ndim 1

guard_fallback.refusal_sweep: 15 crafted refusal cases all returned None (float/np.int64/bool/negative node_count, python lists, float32 weights, int16/uint64/mixed-width/big-endian endpoints, length mismatch, endpoint out of range, negative endpoint, int32 with node_count > int32max, 2-D arrays) (measured)
guard_fallback.silent_domain_widening: none found; the int32 admission is exact and its node_count <= int32max bound is conservative (exactness would hold for larger node_count; the bound only routes extra cases to the identical fallback - performance, not behavior)
guard_fallback.exception_parity_note: at absurd node_count (2**62, 2**63-2, unreachable via public API since node_count comes from node_points.shape[0]) both candidate helper and baseline transcription raise ValueError (bincount minlength vs np.zeros size limits) - parity measured, no divergence; the int32 upcast executes outside the try/except, so OOM during upcast would propagate instead of falling back (bounded at 16 B/edge vs a larger fallback footprint; note-only)
